fragments.fragment_id: 0110_YARuy59msOk_Celine Caruso Dixon - Can We Use AI for Inclusion Work？_0001
fragments.source_video: 0110_YARuy59msOk_Celine Caruso Dixon - Can We Use AI for Inclusion Work？
fragments.text: Hello, everyone. My name is Selen Cruz-Odixson. I am a business analyst who works in policy and governance development in the inclusion space with a keen interest in AI at ATV Financial. And I'd like to welcome you to a conversation on inclusion and AI. When we bring up inclusive language and themes in AI in general, the conversation tends to lean towards the possible biases present in the datasets used for development, biases present in the developers, or even with who is writing the code. And while those aspects of the conversation are necessary in understanding the implications of not having inclusivity or worse ethics in the background, I intend to focus a bit more on how AI impacts us as unique diverse individuals as the end users and as inclusion practitioners.

fragments.fragment_id: 0110_YARuy59msOk_Celine Caruso Dixon - Can We Use AI for Inclusion Work？_0002
fragments.source_video: 0110_YARuy59msOk_Celine Caruso Dixon - Can We Use AI for Inclusion Work？
fragments.text: It has become customary to hear stories on how AI has wronged X group or community. We heard it with artists whose work was stolen for datasets in image generation with facial recognition software that couldn't distinguish between two different individuals of Asian descent and with hiring systems that actively discriminated against women. These are not one-off events nor are they isolated. They tell us something about our societies, how inclusion and existence on equitable terms is lacking and furthermore being exacerbated by AI. Of course, there are good stories too. AI being used to help in cancer research, accessibility tech, and learning as well. However, those harmful stories still persist. And the question arises, how do we use AI to help us on this journey of inclusion? We can't ignore the back end work of developing AI.

fragments.fragment_id: 0110_YARuy59msOk_Celine Caruso Dixon - Can We Use AI for Inclusion Work？_0003
fragments.source_video: 0110_YARuy59msOk_Celine Caruso Dixon - Can We Use AI for Inclusion Work？
fragments.text: As end users and inclusion practitioners, we may not be involved in this development. However, actively questioning who is building AI is necessary if we are to use this technology in the inclusion space. And the same way we vet the resources and education used in this space to make sure it causes as little harm as possible and is overall aiding diverse communities, we must vet the AI systems and tools for the same thing. Furthermore, the intentional curation of datasets that hold inclusion as a central theme rather than as an add-on is integral to the current and future use of AI in our space and communities. Or require in the back end work of AI is the integration of representation in order for AI systems to be used in a more inclusive and diverse way.

fragments.fragment_id: 0110_YARuy59msOk_Celine Caruso Dixon - Can We Use AI for Inclusion Work？_0004
fragments.source_video: 0110_YARuy59msOk_Celine Caruso Dixon - Can We Use AI for Inclusion Work？
fragments.text: Without this crucial step of actually implementing datasets that showcase a wide variety of individuals, communities, and cultures and challenging personally held biases, the possibility of using this technology with an inclusion work becomes more complex. As the implications of using something that could cause harm need to be considered and handled. If we are willing to do that work, however, to use AI, particularly in its current iteration, then another area of using AI in this inclusion space is by bringing it to our communities. As inclusion practitioners, we must recognize the inequality that exists in being able to even access and use this technology. How do we make AI, but also tech as a whole, accessible to the broader communities that exist?

fragments.fragment_id: 0110_YARuy59msOk_Celine Caruso Dixon - Can We Use AI for Inclusion Work？_0005
fragments.source_video: 0110_YARuy59msOk_Celine Caruso Dixon - Can We Use AI for Inclusion Work？
fragments.text: This partially links back to who is building AI. By bringing AI to our communities in an accessible manner, we open a door for them to become the coders, engineers, the developers. It broadens who is working on the back end, making AI a more inclusive space from the start. On the other hand, the possibility of using AI as a tool to help in things like language or culture capturing and revitalization is also something to consider. Take what is happening in Tuvalu as an example, the unfortunate reality of climate change has impacted the island nation of Tuvalu such that it is at risk of being completely wiped off the map in response to this. They have begun the process of becoming the first nation to create a digital twin of itself.

fragments.fragment_id: 0110_YARuy59msOk_Celine Caruso Dixon - Can We Use AI for Inclusion Work？_0006
fragments.source_video: 0110_YARuy59msOk_Celine Caruso Dixon - Can We Use AI for Inclusion Work？
fragments.text: The capturing of the culture, the language, and the people themselves will be used to develop a history of the island nation in an act of radical preservation that has come from the tragedy of losing their home to ever rising sea levels. The loss of language and culture is something that inclusion work comes in contact with regularly. In this way, we can preserve the history of our peoples and communities not as a response to tragedy, but as a way of bringing them to the world. There is a duality that exists here. By bringing AI and more broadly tech to our communities, we are opening up the opportunity for them to get involved in a niche area while at the same time preserving our cultures.

fragments.fragment_id: 0110_YARuy59msOk_Celine Caruso Dixon - Can We Use AI for Inclusion Work？_0007
fragments.source_video: 0110_YARuy59msOk_Celine Caruso Dixon - Can We Use AI for Inclusion Work？
fragments.text: And we can start at any time. We know, for example, that there is a lack of connectivity in indigenous communities across Canada, a crucial part in being able to connect to these AI systems, which means the possibility exists for organizations, corporations, or even individuals to work alongside indigenous peoples to implement connectivity in community. The crucial step for bringing AI into community is that it requires partnership at the base of interaction. We have to build relationships alongside building the confidence to use AI in community. This also brings up a much larger question for us to consider, which is who is AI for. I thought in the sense of what is the use case of particular AI tech, but more so who as end users can use this technology as a benefit to their lives rather than an impediment.

fragments.fragment_id: 0110_YARuy59msOk_Celine Caruso Dixon - Can We Use AI for Inclusion Work？_0008
fragments.source_video: 0110_YARuy59msOk_Celine Caruso Dixon - Can We Use AI for Inclusion Work？
fragments.text: When I ask who is AI for, I'm asking about the use of use and understanding about its integration into society or communities, about the representation of who end users are. But also, if it is only for the privileged few who will have the time, money, and ability to understand and use AI. We've seen that AI tech can specialize in accessibility, but that doesn't mean all AI tech is accessible. And we've seen that AI has gone through the process of vetting data sets to be more inclusive, but once again, that doesn't mean all AI tech does that. When we look at the broader scope of AI tech, we can see how there aren't very many that would fit into a more inclusive category for who their end user are.

fragments.fragment_id: 0110_YARuy59msOk_Celine Caruso Dixon - Can We Use AI for Inclusion Work？_0009
fragments.source_video: 0110_YARuy59msOk_Celine Caruso Dixon - Can We Use AI for Inclusion Work？
fragments.text: However, that doesn't mean that we can't use AI tech, just that it becomes much more difficult to. This is something that we need to consider when we work with AI, especially when we bring it into communities, because of the harm and discomfort that it can bring alongside it. There is a very large difference in being uncomfortable because of a growth opportunity and being uncomfortable because you're not considered or wanted. So it's something to constantly keep at the forefront. As a tool, AI can help us be more inclusive overall. One method and bias mitigation, for example, is using AI as a filtering mechanism. Having an AI system filter out information such as names, gender, birth dates, names of educational institutions, et cetera, et cetera, creates an anonymous candidate that has equal opportunity.

fragments.fragment_id: 0110_YARuy59msOk_Celine Caruso Dixon - Can We Use AI for Inclusion Work？_0010
fragments.source_video: 0110_YARuy59msOk_Celine Caruso Dixon - Can We Use AI for Inclusion Work？
fragments.text: It also allows us to question what is truly necessary in our hiring process. What is the difference between individuals that have computer science degrees from different accredited universities, for example. The bias group that occurs from the mention of an esteemed or highly regarded university is very real. The key here is that AI is not handling who the most acceptable candidate for the position is. Rather, it handles smaller pieces of information removal with the larger decision remaining in the hands of the individuals. The way to use AI and inclusion work is not by having a human in the loop, but rather by having an AI in the loop. This is because inclusion work is critically human.

fragments.fragment_id: 0110_YARuy59msOk_Celine Caruso Dixon - Can We Use AI for Inclusion Work？_0011
fragments.source_video: 0110_YARuy59msOk_Celine Caruso Dixon - Can We Use AI for Inclusion Work？
fragments.text: It requires us to be fully present and consider ourselves, our peers, and the society at large. So by switching to having AI in the loop, we remove the responsibility that is placed into AI's hands and return it to the individuals. It's important to consider who holds responsibility if a mistake arises in these situations. Because if AI is the one responsible for making impactful decisions in this space, it allows us to make excuses for the mistake that occurs. We can say always a software or the coding or just wasn't built correctly for this task, we can try again with something else. In doing this, we remove the responsibility from ourselves and essentially place it in the hands of the AI, which effectively is a system that is built from the data on our society.

fragments.fragment_id: 0110_YARuy59msOk_Celine Caruso Dixon - Can We Use AI for Inclusion Work？_0012
fragments.source_video: 0110_YARuy59msOk_Celine Caruso Dixon - Can We Use AI for Inclusion Work？
fragments.text: It is showing us the biases that already exist in it in a much more apparent way. As practitioners of inclusion, we must hold the responsibility of our work in our own hands and only allow AI to be a useful tool. Going back to that idea of having an AI in the loop, rather than a human in the loop. It can be used to help advance our work, but it's how we use it, the role we give it that will ultimately dictate the end results. Through all of this, however, it's important to know that this is an ever changing conversation, much like the inclusion field. So we must hold space for these conversations and the many possibilities that could arise from them.

fragments.fragment_id: 0110_YARuy59msOk_Celine Caruso Dixon - Can We Use AI for Inclusion Work？_0013
fragments.source_video: 0110_YARuy59msOk_Celine Caruso Dixon - Can We Use AI for Inclusion Work？
fragments.text: An example I often enjoy considering is the use of AGI in the space. A sentient AI that is able to make its own decisions would change the way that we interacted. From an ethical standpoint, it may no longer be considered a tool, but another being an actualized agent. That in and of itself brings in the question of rights and ethical existence for an AI, a specialization that may one day exist in our field alongside those who specialize in accessibility, cultural representation and gender equality. As these conversations and fields shift at what seems like ever increasing speeds, new possibilities will arise from them. It gives rise to concerns as we've discussed, which will need to be handled transparently by both fields, but it also gives rise to a never ending list of possibilities.

fragments.fragment_id: 0110_YARuy59msOk_Celine Caruso Dixon - Can We Use AI for Inclusion Work？_0014
fragments.source_video: 0110_YARuy59msOk_Celine Caruso Dixon - Can We Use AI for Inclusion Work？
fragments.text: And I believe that together we can develop a hyper technological future that is as inclusive and as equitable as we treatment to make it. Thank you so much for listening today, and please feel free to reach out to discuss this area or anything else in inclusion at AGI further.
